Of the 77 stored cap hits a forced commit is right on 0-2 at every N. Of the 184 answers over 8,000 tokens, 28 are right when forced, 40 when left alone; the commit keeps 24 of those 40. title: No text sign predicts a failing Think-SFT sample early
what: Six label-free text signs read at token 4,000 to 12,000 do not tell a failing Think-SFT sample from a right one of the same problem: best AUROC 0.568 [0.480, 0.657]. Stopping at the first sign saves 0.8 % of tokens on hard328, not 10 %.
why: Cap hits are 29 to 46 % of Think-SFT's samples; a perfect detector at token 4,000 would give 244 of 328 at 16,250 tokens against 241 at 30,837. Text signs do not provide it (as result-f3d708, result-b30f15).
caveat: Replay on stored rows, not a new run. One hand reader. The 32,768 result is one sample per problem. Only 29 samples have switched by token 8,000.
Details. Signs: switch to a non-Latin script, repeated 50-token windows, loop rule A, zlib ratio, 'wait', restart phrases; 213 to 348 within-problem pairs on hard328 + fresh2026, every interval covers 0.5. Stop rule chosen on MATH-500: tokens saved 0.8 % [-0.3, 1.8] on hard328 and 1.1 % [-0.1, 2.4] on fresh2026 for -0.5 right (24 orders).
Description: 156 of 1,312 Think-SFT samples on hard328 and 104 of 544 on fresh2026 switch script (RL 12 and 9, base 9 and 6); 98 % of the letters are Chinese; median first switch at token 13,589; English resumes after 85 % of first episodes. Hand read of 20 (by the agent): 15 continue the same working with Chinese connectives, 4 are one stray word, 1 gives up and guesses. Within problem a switch by 8,000 changes the right rate by +5.3 points [-2.0, 13.3] (25 problems). In the 32,768 sample, cut answers that switched before 16,384 finish right 1 of 24 against 22 of 69 (-24.0 points [-36.8, -10.6] inside strata of the base's right count).

title: Tier list of novel findings: the finish dial is first
what: 103 read-only agents collected 144 distinct findings from the whole project; the top 30 were re-read at their artifacts and tiered by 5 judges, the top 10 checked against the web. All are new measurements on known phenomena.
why: The judges agree on one reading: finishing and being right when finished are separate directions in weight space; RL moved the first, imitation supplies the second.
caveat: EXA_API_KEY is unset on this laptop: 24 of 30 first novelty checks used paper notes only; the top 10 were redone with web search. The other 114 findings were not re-read at their artifacts.
S: finish dial (result-6f1bb7, result-95a4dc), judges 4.8 of 5. Size of 8 RL directions sets cap hits 96, 77, 50, 46, 25, 5 at sizes -1 to 2 on the 328; random rank-8 flat. Published: low-rank RL delta carries the gain (AlphaRL 2510.00553, RELEX 2605.21468). Not found: the readout as finishing, the random control, k=8 beating k=1 on hard problems.
A: delta transplant Think-SFT + 2 x (RL - base), 231.5 of 328 (result-3387ce), 4.2. Web check: SFT + about 2 x RL delta beating both parents is published (DoTS 2605.00610, coefficients 1.82 and 1.54); drop 'peak at 2x' as the novelty. Ours: cap hits 94.5 to 33 while right-of-finished falls 88.0 to 71.5 %, and the Gaussian control at 0.0.
A: Think-SFT + cue beats RL on 136 problems from 2026, vote 75 vs 57 (result-5251c9), 4.0. The ordering is published (2505.14216); ours is the error split: 80.4 % of finished answers right vs 42.8 % for RL.
B (3.0 to 3.4): Think-SFT wins the 328 by abstaining at the cap; base opens itself (411 vs cue 410); 8 directions write the cue (430 of 500 open 'Okay'); step 100 installs the opening; the reliability split also appears for base-vs-base and a random weight change; theories no nearer than no-theory readers (182 of 370); prefix hand-off; steering 'Wait' adds nothing.

1. Brief-reasoning sentence after the prompt (". Keep your reasoning brief and to the point: once you have the answer, state it and stop"): within-run A/B of 500 samples per arm, 262 vs 258 right, 452k vs 580k tokens. Same per-sample accuracy for 22 % fewer tokens. Untested with the cue. Refuted if accuracy per sample drops with the cue.

2. Two-pass vote under a token budget: 12 samples capped at 1,536 tokens; then only truncated samples that do not loop are continued (+2,560), and only for problems where fewer than 60 % of samples agree. 84.0 mean of 7 runs at 10,800 tokens per problem. It is a token-level form of our sequential vote: stop a problem when the vote is clear, not when two samples agree.

3. Half-vote guess for a sample that never finishes: at the first cap, append "\n\nAnswer:" and read 24 tokens; the guess votes with weight 0.5 only if the sample has no answer at the end. On the same seeds 83 and 83 with guesses against 81 without. Differs from our closing cue (result-51fd20, negative): the guess never replaces a finished answer and counts half inside a vote.

4. Within-run A/B as the instrument: split the samples of ONE run into two arms and compare right samples per arm (n 500 to 600 per arm) instead of comparing two run scores of n 100. It separated temperature 0.3 from 0.9 (294 vs 221) where run scores could not.

5. Plain prompt, per sample: T 0.3 beats 0.9 (294 vs 221 of 500) and 0.6 (294 vs 250); T 0.2 beats 0.4 (307 vs 274) but hard problems then get no finished sample (loops). The opposite direction to the cued base, where T 1.0 wins.

6. Cheap loop test before spending tokens on a continuation: the last 120 characters occur earlier in the text.

Negatives it found: repetition penalty 1.1 (249 vs 293 right samples), top-p 0.8 against 0.95 (309 vs 306, more tokens), a Solution heading before the answer (266 vs 283), a vote weighted by sample length (no gain, though the winning group is the longer one in 55 of 62 right problems), 16 short samples instead of 12 (hard problems need the long ones).

Slip-hazard law for the RL gain: an answer is a chain of steps each with a small chance of an unrecovered slip, P(right) = exp(-h L_i); a method multiplies h by a constant (RL about 0.4x). Laptop only.

Where does low temperature help and where does it loop? (for hard328; config chosen on MATH-500). Facts: cued base at T 0.6 is more accurate when it finishes (378 vs ~362 at T 1.0 on the same 402 MATH-500 problems, knowledge-13cff3) but loops on 98/500; min-p 0.1 at T 1.0 also raises finished accuracy (404/442 vs 410/473) and brings loops back (result-44b4df). Both sharpen every position. Test: a per-token rule in a vLLM logits processor, logits/T_low only where next-token entropy H is above h0 (the top 20 % of positions, 'forking tokens' of 2506.01939), T 1.0 elsewhere; 2x2 with the reverse gate, constant T_low and T 1.0, T_low in {0.6, 0.3}. Hypothesis: loops come from sharpening confident positions (the tail tokens there are the exits from a repeated block), accuracy from sharpening forks. Refuted if the forks-only arm has cap hits at the T 0.6 level, or no more right than T 1.0. Either outcome says which positions carry the T 0.6 gain. Then the winner once on the 328, both models. Not the loop-triggered temperature boost (llama.cpp PR 22007): no loop detector, the gate is the entropy alone.

Policy improvement at decoding time, no weights and no reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-46b68c). Thesis: what is left of the RL gain is reliability, not knowledge: any of 4 base samples is right on 467/500 (MATH-500) and 205/328 (hard328, = RL single 206), and RL stores in weights the choice a critic could make while decoding. Replace the weights by a critic read from the base's own activations, trained with no answer key (target: will this sample agree with the plurality of 4), and use it to stop a failing sample early and start again. Differs from idea-0d55a4 (vote as a reward for weight updates) and from the length rules (result-2c2cae: +0.9 to +3.7 pts at up to 2.2x tokens): no weight changes, and the critic acts before the length is known. Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: accuracy and tokens of stop-and-restart with a perfect critic at 10/25/50 % of the answer; stop if it cannot reach 440/500 at <= 1.5x tokens. Stage 1, one forward job: probe on base residual activations at 10/25/50 % of the 2,000 stored MATH-500 samples, 5 folds by problem, AUROC for plurality agreement and (evaluation only) correctness, vs tokens so far, mean log-prob and entropy so far. Stop if AUROC at 25 % is within 0.03 of the best of those. Stage 2: threshold chosen on MATH-500, scored once on hard328 for base and RL with tokens per problem; target base >= 190/328 at <= 1.3x tokens (theta(0.5) 190, RL 206). Stage 3 only if stage 2 gains: at the 10 % highest-entropy positions score the top tokens with the critic and compare the choices with the tokens Math-RL prefers (score_tokens instrument, result-edceef step 2). Against it: result-f21d2e (no J-lens feature beats length for a wrong base answer, AUROC 0.831), 2608.17124 and 2605.09502 (the correctness direction is a readout, steering with it does not help), 2504.05419 (probes for own correctness exist, on trained reasoning models). Checked today on 500 stored base answers: the summed log-ratio log p_RL - log p_base separates right from wrong at AUROC 0.853, the same as length alone (0.855), and the per-token mean does not favour right answers, so the RL model's likelihood is not a usable critic.

RL-Zero without the reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-607778). Thesis: one RL sample is the base's own 4-sample vote paid once in weights. Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: among problems where no base sample of 4 is right, how often is RL right; and when the base plurality is wrong, how often RL gives the same wrong answer. Thesis refuted if RL is right on more than half of the pass@4 failures. Stage 1, one GPU job: gradient of log-prob of the stored base samples with sign +1 for plurality-agreeing finished samples and -1 for minority and cap-hit samples; no answer key. Measure its top-8 subspace overlap and cosine with the RL-Math delta against a random null and against the same gradient built with the true key (ceiling). Stage 2: base + one step of that gradient at the norm of 0.25 (RL - base); cue, hard328, vs base 164, theta0.25 182, RL 206. Controls: matched-norm random (417-level null), sign flipped, positives only, true-key. Known against it: 2509.04259 (on-policy data matters, not negatives), 2607.13643 and 2505.14216 (SFT on own agreeing or correct answers gives < 1 pt), a wrong plurality gets reinforced. Published neighbour: TTRL uses vote as an online reward; not done from a base model beside a released RL-Zero delta, and no one-step alignment test.

Reward content test: does the MATH-500 gain need a math reward, a reasoning reward, or only RL from the base? AI2 released RL-Zero models from the same base for 5 rewards (names read from HF 02:18 UTC): Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-IF, -General, -Mix, -Code, -Math, plus 3.1 Code and Math. We have 2 points: Code-RL cue 450 vs Math-RL cue 457 of 500, weight differences cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f). Step 1, about 5 cells, 9 USD: IF, General, Mix (and 3.0 Math, Code as same-version controls), cue and plain, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, same run_cell. Baselines: base cue 410, random difference 417, theta(0.25) 441, RL 457. Step 2, forward only: teacher-force base, each RL model, the random difference and theta(0.25) on the same 2,000 stored base answers (job 208b); per token r_m = log p_m - log p_base. Measure the correlation of r across models over positions, and at the 10 percent of positions with the largest |r_Math| whether the other models prefer the same token (2603.22117: replacing those 10 percent of tokens gives the full RL score). Null: the random difference, and Math 3.0 vs 3.1 as the ceiling. Readings: IF cue >= 441 and r_IF agrees with r_Math far above the random null means the gain is the same set of token decisions whatever the reward, so it is a property of the base model, and the next step is to predict those positions from the base alone (label-free). IF cue <= 420 with Code at 450 means the reward must grade a reasoning task. Equal scores with r uncorrelated means different decisions reach the same score. Not published: 2608.03573 reports orthogonal RL updates across tasks and no harm to other tasks, 2509.01363 Sec 4.4 a +2 pt cross-task gain with no control, 2610.24663 and 2603.22117 use one RL model each; none compares token decisions across rewards. Check each model's base and tensor layout on its card before any merge.

RL gain as context: does a context window carry what the RL weight difference carries? Base + cue, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, grader v3, n 500, same run_cell harness with a longer prefix. Prefix = 3 solved problems from MATH train (none in MATH-500 or the 328), each about 1,500 tokens, in the test template, then the test problem and the cue. Arms differ only in who wrote the 3 answers: (i) cued base, picked without an answer key (4 samples agree, finished), (ii) Math-RL 3.1, (iii) Code-RL 3.1, (iv) control: cued base answers picked at random, same token count. Baselines: base cue 410, theta(0.25) cue 441, RL cue 457. Arm (v), only if (ii) < 441: 16 trainable prefix vectors fit by KL to RL's next-token distribution on RL's MATH-train answers (no reward), as the upper bound of any context. Why: a=0.25 plain (405) equals the cue (410), both RL deltas read out the cue token (result-e2482e), Code-RL gives the math gain with cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f), and 2505.14216 Table 1 finds SFT on RL's answers gives +11.6 pts while SFT on the base's own correct answers gives +0.8: the gain is in how RL writes, not in correctness. Not tested in context on a base model (Wang 2610.06851 tests only RL's opening of the same problem, 77.7 = cue). Readings: (i) >= 430 is a label-free route with no RL model at all; (ii) >= 441 with (i),(iv) <= 420 means 3 pasted RL answers carry the gain, then run the same 3 answers on a base model of another family that has no RL release; all arms <= 420 and (v) < 441 refutes: context cannot carry it. Generated tokens are equal by design; prompt tokens are reported. Cost: 4 cells, forward only, about 4 USD. Choose on MATH-500, score the best arm once on the 328.

Label-free selection among the cued base's own samples is the open problem on hard328: any of 4 samples right on 205 of 328 (62.5 %), which equals RL's single answer (206), but a plurality vote of the 4 reaches 179 and length rules 163-172. On the 246 paired problems pass@4 is 157 for the base against 148 for RL single. A selector that needs no answer key and recovers half of the 26 problems between vote@4 and pass@4 would put the cued base at RL's level at 4x tokens. Rows exist (work-140e13). Closest published: self-certainty and prefix-confidence selection are at or below majority vote on MATH500 (2507.18122 Table 1); 2502.18581 claims the opposite (unread). From work-a992bd.

Workspace steering, data-backed (follows idea-42e9ea): add J-lens vectors of Wait/Hmm/perhaps and subtract EOS/Answer/So at layers 20-28 of the cued base while it solves MATH-500. Controls: norm-matched random direction; the same bias on output logits. Refuted if <= both controls.

From interp_research next (04_PRACTICAL.md K2, not run): merge the Math-RL and Code-RL deltas, with RL-Zero-Mix as the ceiling. Hackathon form: base + a*(Math-RL - base) + b*(Code-RL - base) for (a, b) in {(1,1), (0.5,0.5), (1,0.5)}, plus TIES and DARE merges at the same parameter count, against allenai Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Mix (check the exact HF name and that it starts from Olmo-3-1025-7B), scored on MATH-500 (cue, T 1.0) and on the Code pair's benchmark with the same harness. Reuses the merge step and both deltas that work-d36669 already loads. Question: does one weight-space model hold both RL gains, and how much does adding the Code delta cost or add on math? Refuted (no interference) if (1,1) is within 2 SE of Math-RL on MATH-500 and of Code-RL on code; the card's own refutation is for its neuron-level merge (within the seed band of TIES or DARE). Critique: (1) the card's neuron-level version (merge each task's top-k neurons) is undercut by N13 (knowledge-8229be): top-k neurons carry none of the math gain, so merge whole deltas or DARE samples. (2) In team memory, 2606.18521: a code-RL model scores above a math-RL one on MATH (DeepCoder-1.5B 57.32 % vs DeepScaleR-1.5B 52.84 %), so Code-RL is not a zero control; task arithmetic of two 7B math-RLVR deltas scored 54.28 % (Table 4): interference can be large. (3) work-d36669's cos(Code, RL) job measures the overlap first; sameraslan's layer-31 smoke reads cos 0.040 (work-f374ef). Cost: about 6 merged models, one MATH-500 cell each on Modal H100.

From interp_research next (20_ABSTRACT.md, 'The highest-leverage next step'; not run): rank test of the RL delta. For each MLP matrix of Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math minus Olmo-3-1025-7B, add a rank-r truncation (SVD; r = 16, 64, 256) to the base, against a random subspace of equal rank and equal energy, MATH-500 (here: T 1.0, cue, run_cell.py; MLP-only so it compares with N13's whole-MLP arm, 86.4 at T 0.6), GSM8K held out on the rank-64 pair. Hypothesis: the gain sits in a low-rank part of each matrix's change (rank-64 within 2 SE of the whole-MLP arm). Refuted if rank-64 scores at the random-subspace control. Why now: N13 (knowledge-8229be) showed no neuron subset carries the gain but a 0.1 % DARE sample does; rank separates 'low-rank' from 'spread evenly'. Practical if it holds: r x (d+n) numbers per matrix for transplant or merging with the Code-RL delta. Cost estimate in the file: 6 arms, 12-16 GPU-h on L40S under N13's harness (SVD not costed); the same 6 arms on Modal H100 at T 1.0 are each one MATH-500 cell. Critique: priors point against low rank in energy (2505.11711: update nearly full rank; 2611.11752: OLMo-2-7B PPO update needs 2,120 of 4,096 components for 80 % energy at L16 down-proj), but energy rank is not functional rank, and 2605.21468 reports rank-1 trajectory extrapolation works. Also cited in interp_research next/04_RECENT.md, abstracts only: 2610.22438 (counted rank of 13 released fine-tuning updates up to 8B is only a little below a random matrix of the same shape) and 2609.22146 GRRR (removing the change of singular values keeps most math gains). WSP-1 (work-f374ef) computes singular spectra but does not score truncations. Use stochastic rounding into bf16 (work-d36669 found 54 % of delta entries <= 1 bf16 ulp).

Exploration-collapse testbed: reproduce Fork-and-Flush (2610.07447) vs single run vs best-of-4 at matched submissions on a cheap CPU task (circles26), gpt-5.4-mini agents via OpenAI API, basin maps of each arm. Code studies/explore, branch ali/basins.

gpuprice prior-fitted network on synthetic rate-card markets (not started; literature subagent still reading): simulator of sticky posted prices with entry/exit and undercutting, train a small transformer to emit the median's quantiles from 60 days of listing context; real data is test only. Scales with compute, no real training data needed.

gpuprice open-weights LLM as the density over the provider panel (running, subagent): prompt = 21 days of every listing's price as a table, sample 30 answers for the median at t+h, read q10/q50/q90. Refuted if <= lve on the same cells. Evidence: Context is Key, Llama-3.1-405B 0.159 RCRPS with context vs 0.473 without, Chronos-Large 0.326. Leak rule: weights released before 2026-10, no tools.

gpuprice foundation model at the listing level (running, subagent): amazon/chronos-2 zero-shot per series, with all 37 as one group, spread-only, and per LISTING with the median taken over joint draws. Refuted if <= +0.126 (lve). Prior against: top models gain +0.06..+0.14 over naive on M4-daily; fine-tuning small data worsens Chronos-2 0.423 -> 0.477.

gpuprice simulator v2 (running, subagent): per-provider repricing behaviour instead of pooled, hazard by time since last change, mixture with the median's own change at h=1, pooled rolling calibration to 0.80 in-band. Refuted if dev pooled skill <= +0.197 (it01-sim). Evidence: Brown-MacKay rates 0.01-1.89 changes/product/day; Cavallo hump-shaped hazard; pack: Verda 40-42 change days, CoreWeave 0.

gpuprice FX pass-through: Scaleway's posted USD price = fixed EUR price x previous day's ECB EUR/USD rate (d-log correlation 0.985, n=86, H100 80GB and B300; subagent test). So the h=1 price of those listings is known at the origin, and h=3/7 is an FX random walk. Add to the listing simulator as a per-listing rule. Also: Verda reprices on 40-42 of 60-89 days (dynamic), CoreWeave/Hyperstack/Modal/Together never: per-provider hazard, not pooled. Extra history: fastgpu HF git commit cc6358f4 (+30 days, CC BY 4.0), adriannutiu/gpu-rental-prices git (+30 days).

Workspace injection: add J-lens vectors of the RL-diff tokens to the base residual at workspace layers (38-92 % depth) during generation, 100 MATH-500 problems. Controls: norm-matched random direction, random-token lens vectors. Prior: lens writes are weak (19 % vs 75 % trained vectors).

Lens-gated check cue: use the base's own J-lens readout to decide WHEN to insert a short check phrase (as the opening cue does once). Offline test first: does the readout predict positions where RL's token differs from base's better than output entropy? Refuted if AUROC <= entropy.

J-lens workspace diff, base vs RL: teacher-force saved T1/T2 MATH-500 answers through both models, read mid-layer J-lens (fitted lens exists for base), list tokens RL holds that base lacks on the 65 RL-only problems vs 398 both-right. Forward only, ~1 H100-h. Null: shuffled pairs.

Weight-space programming edits (knowledge-c9fc18) on the cued base, label-free contrasts only: mean-activation direction of (a) cap-hit vs finished answers, (b) short vs long answers (ThinkEdit 2503.22048), (c) garbled vs boxed final line, projected out of / added to MLP-out or head-out weights. Ceiling from result-5e17a6: 16+13+8 problems = 7.4 pts; published edits give 0-1 pt on MATH-500 when the model does not loop. Refuted if no edit gains > 3.4 pts on the 500.

No-reward weight delta: base + a*(Olmo-3-7B-Think-SFT - base), a in {0.25,0.5,1,1.5}, final and early step branches (step1000..), cue prefilled, MATH-500 T 1.0, same harness as idea-2eb58d. Tests whether an imitation-only delta carries the 10.6 points RL adds. Refuted if no a beats 82.0 by > 3.4 pts (2 SE). Check special-token diff first (knowledge-38042f).

Strategy basins base vs RL: blind LLM judge groups 32 samples per problem by method, 42 MATH-500 problems, base+cue vs RL at T 1.0. Main number: share of RL's correct answers in strategies the base never used. Prior: Lee 2606.29985 Tab 2. Code: branch ali/strategy-basins. Needs GPU.

Code-RL model on MATH-500 with and without the cue (one cell each, T 1.0): is the remaining 10.6 points specific to a math reward? 2610.06851 Table 6 has the reverse case only: the 3.0 Math-RL model scores 68.5 on HumanEval, cued base 69.8, base 50.2, and it has no Code-RL model. If Code-RL with the plain prompt is near 92 on MATH-500, the residual is task-general; if it is near the cued base (82), it is math-specific. This is the model-level version of the Code-RL control in the weight-difference study (idea-2eb58d) and costs 2 cells. Check the exact Code-RL model name on Hugging Face first. From work-2aaf3a.

Disagreement map after the cue: score the existing 500 T1 and 500 T2 answers token by token under both models (teacher forcing, 4 passes, no sampling). Question: once the cue is given, where does Olmo-3.1 RL still disagree with the base? Prediction from the T1/T2 item table: on the base's 23 wrong answers under 4,000 tokens, RL gives low probability to the token where the base starts its final answer (RL has 0 wrong answers under 4,000 tokens and its right answers are 2.1x longer, median 3,014 vs 1,432). Closest published: 2610.24663 Table 3 and App. E, 2605.06241 Table 2 (Qwen pairs, plain base, no cue; RL differs at 1-4 % of positions). Differs in Olmo pair, cued prefix, the 3.1 model, and the test at the answer position. Refuted if RL's probability of the base's answer-start token is within 2x of the base's, or if disagreement is uniform over position. Also gives the per-position data for the weight-difference study. From work-2aaf3a.

Stop at a length cutoff and restart (both models, T 1.0), cutoff chosen on MATH-500. T1: above 12,000 tokens the cued base has 15 right and 40 wrong answers; stopping there frees 329 tokens per problem. RL: 16 right, 22 wrong above 12,000. None of the base's 27 cap hits is a loop (rule A fires on 0 of 500): they are reasoning that does not converge, and RL solves 16 of them in a median of 8,594 tokens. The T 0.6 restart row recovered 60 of 119 cap hits. Closest published: 2601.11940 (restart at a matched budget of 4, UNREAD) and our K_fresh row; differs in T 1.0, cut by length instead of the cap, RL given the same rule, tokens counted. Refuted if the net gain at equal tokens is <= 0 for the base or equal for both models. From work-2aaf3a.

Double-check short answers at equal tokens (cued base, T 1.0). T1 data: base answers of <= 2,000 tokens are 263 of 500 and 13 are wrong; RL has 0 wrong among its 286 answers of <= 4,000 tokens. Procedure: when the first answer is <= 2,000 tokens, draw a second sample; if the two final answers differ, draw a third and take the majority. Cost ~514 extra tokens per problem, so base stays under RL's mean (3,933 + 514 vs 4,694). RL gets the same procedure (expected gain 0). Closest published: Maj@2/4 in 2507.18122 Table 1 and majority@k in 2610.06851 Fig. 21; differs in gating by length, matching tokens to RL, cued base. Refuted if fewer than 8 of the 13 are recovered (errors repeat across samples) or new errors offset them. Then the 328. From work-2aaf3a.

past.dev Multi-Agent Memory Challenge brief (sponsor PDF linked from iterate.inc/ai-research resources, read Nov 14): the judge scores 1 to 5 on A real swarm (more than one agent, real writes and reads between agents, a read boundary that stays correct when tested), A memory design with reasons (why each layer, and the result expected before the run), Evidence (a trace in which one agent uses data from a different agent; a failure with its explanation), Honesty (caveats in the README). Required: README section 'past.dev challenge' with headings Agents, Layers, Results, Caveats, and in the demo one read in which an agent uses data from a different agent. Our page: /pastdev (tools/pastdev.py). Open gaps in our README: no read boundary inside past.dev, and no expected result written before the run.

Exa challenge brief (sponsor PDF linked from iterate.inc/ai-research resources, read Nov 14): judged on Exa is central 30% ('the project would break, or get clearly worse, without search'), Research value 25%, Creativity 25% ('a use of search we haven't seen before'), Checkable output 20% ('results trace back to real sources, and it works in a live demo'). Required: at least one Exa API call in the project's main loop, a repo link pointing to where Exa is called, and a demo that shows what the system found through Exa and how it used it. Our page: /exa (tools/exa_page.py), README section Exa challenge.

Round 09 restated two of the seven: problems-m06 restates run-07/f2-m05, stopping-m05 restates run-02/f2-m05.

Published: 'probes read the problem, not the attempt'. Bulut, arXiv 2609.03436 (R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, MATH, 256 samples per problem): pooled probe AUROC 0.849 at token 4, within-problem 0.496 [0.466, 0.527], to 512 tokens. Our critic result (0.57 within, 0.73-0.77 across) replicates it on a base model at 1,000-2,000 tokens; new in ours: text signs, the stop-and-restart policy priced against random stopping, the perfect-critic ceiling = RL. Do not claim the control as new.

Theory round 08 refuted 2 theories on stored rows. r8-m02 (cued base loses answers by switching lines of attack; RL switches less): base/RL switch-marker rate per token 0.758 (n 497, 90 % [0.71, 0.80]) vs predicted 1.6 [1.15, 2.4]; RL switches more per token. Replication timed out (600 s), not replicated. r3-across-2 (base leaves loops only via low-probability tail tokens; RL adds a constant push toward 'Wait'/'Hmm'): p5 0.179 (n 473, [0.02, 0.30]) vs 0.62 [0.42, 0.85], replicated. Also r8-m09 (Think-SFT 'Answer:' layout at a fixed rate per answer) loses its duel -3.05 nats on 2 separating tests: the layout is used on short, easy answers (duel p2 0.35, n 20, vs 0.95 [0.6, 1.45]). Artifacts: studies/theory/results/engine/round-08/metrics_v4.json, metrics_v5.json, commit d98e2c2.

Not run: 'extrapolate the first 100 RL steps' (scale step-100's directions to reach final RL). Two reasons. (1) It is published for other models, abstracts only read: RELEX 2605.21468 (rank-1 subspace from ~50 RLVR steps, extrapolated 10-20x, matches full RLVR on Qwen 1.5-8B), AlphaRL 2510.00553 (rank-1 of the RL update, early-window extrapolation), 2601.04537 (linear RLVR weight dynamics); counterpoint NExt 2604.11446 (rank-1 subspace does not evolve linearly). (2) Our stored weights argue against its strong form for Olmo 3: step-100 vs final change of RL-Math 3.1 has cosine 0.099, top-8 overlap 0.247 input side and 0.087 output side (random 0.002), and only 3.1% of step-100's change lies in the final top-8 input subspace; Code 3.1: 0.135, 0.301, 0.119, 4.8%; Math 3.0: 0.116, 0.398, 0.122. So the input subspace is partly set by step 100 (enough to name the reward), the direction of the change is not. Caveat: step-100's change is 0.028% of the weight norm, near BF16 rounding, which lowers cosines. Artifact: studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/overlap_steps-01/readout.json (tables cos, overlap_right, overlap_left, cap_right). Open and cheap if someone wants the model-specific test: base + step-100 top-8 at the final top-8 norm (about 9x) on hard328.

Theory round 07 (engine 7.1), numbers computed from stored rows (studies/theory/results/engine/round-07/metrics_v4.json): refuted (1) 'the cued base's arithmetic slips are single T 1.0 draws of a wrong number token': its self-inconsistent-equation rate at T 1.0 is 0.36 times the rate at T 0.6 (n 377; predicted 3). (2) 'RL-written examples help only in their own subject': same-subject minus other-subject gain is -0.018 (n 223, 90 % [-0.058, 0.022]). Five more theories gained nothing over the no-theory readers (generic-problem prior, Code-RL as a veto, 3.0 stops at 12k, Think-SFT final format, shared-context wrong values), mostly on groups of 6 to 55 items. 5 of 12 mechanisms were abandoned as already contradicted by the board. The one open experiment (vote over 4 with a plain-sample tie-break) is predicted at 450 of 500 by both sides, below the best known 454: not worth running.

Theory round 06, refuted theories (numbers computed from stored rows and recomputed; studies/theory/results/engine/round-06/metrics_v4.json): (1) the first 100 RL steps bring only opening, format and length: step 100's finished answers are already 4.6 points more often right than the cued base's on the same MATH-500 problems at T 0.6 (n 345, 90 % [2.6, 6.7]). (2) RL's 'Wait'/'Hmm' excess is a timer since the last result: far/near ratio 0.97, and near a result RL already has 1.38 times the base's rate. (3) the cued base's register fades far from the cue: 0.7 % of its hard328 answers of 12,000+ tokens have a textbook header in the second half (n 136). (4) intermediate Think-SFT doses hit the cap more than the ends: no bump, and at a = 0.25 only 0.065 of the log length change has arrived. (5) early answer markers cause the base's quick wrong answers: 0 of 13. Also from the duels: 0.8 % of the plain base's wrong non-self-opened T 1.0 answers have a right first answer marker (n 260), so its loss is not a last-marker grading artifact. Untested: r6-m06 (no per-token probabilities in stored hard328 rows). 6 of 12 mechanisms were abandoned by their developers as already contradicted by the board.

Closed routes for 'catch or avoid a wrong base sample while it is being written, no label, no second model' (cued base, MATH-500, all on main, studies/rlneurons README 'Critic at decoding time' and 'Wrong steps'). Early detectors, within-problem AUROC right vs wrong at 1,000 tokens: linear probe on activations 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] (result-b30f15); base's own mean log p 0.519; problem dependence log p(tok|problem) - log p(tok|no problem) 0.531 [0.468, 0.589] (result-f3d708); RL's likelihood of the base text is length only (0.853 vs 0.855). Bound: a perfect detector at 1,000 tokens gives 438.7/500 against 410.5, so even a working one stays below the vote (446). Steering: problem contrast (context-aware decoding) from before the wrong step +1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8], gains above 8 excluded (result-a497ff); T 0.6 raises the wrong steps. What did hold: Math-RL is half as likely to write the base's wrong step (D -0.71 nats); a misreading has cost 32 points before its sentence (result-c495fe); RL capped rows already hold a boxed answer in 69 % of cases, base capped rows in 17 %. Not tested: detectors trained across problems on more data; contrast from the first answer token on a full cell (expected gain under 2 points, below what n 500 resolves).

On the 328 the base-to-RL gap is not a selection problem. Vote over 4: RL right and base wrong on 36 problems; the base has a right sample among its four on only 10 of them, none on 26. A perfect selector over the base's four samples (pass@4 = 207) only equals one RL sample (207); the base's vote loses 15 problems to selection, RL's 19. Base-only wins: 7. Neither model: 100 under the vote, 79 with any right sample after restarts. So better voting or tie rules cannot close the gap here; it needs answers the base never writes (weights or longer reasoning: see Think-SFT, cap 32,768). Source: per_problem in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/readout.json and hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/readout.json (result-5c961a).

Grader v3 scores an 'Answer:' line wrong when an algebraic answer ends with a period ('15x - 80.' against gold '15x - 80'; numbers and $..$. are accepted). Size, counted on committed MATH-500 rows by regrading with the period removed: base cue 4 samples 0 of 2,137 rows, RL 4 samples 1 of 2,041 ('√53.'), egate hi6 1 of 1,000, lo6 2 of 2,000, esc3k 0 of 500. At most 0.1 point in any cell and no base-against-RL bias, so no posted number changes; a grader v5 is not worth a rescore for this alone. Found while reviewing result-34897a.

Literature for 'RL first installs the cue's opening' and for label-free RL, read 2026-11-15 (findings in tools/paper.py). (1) Per-checkpoint cue curve is unpublished: 2610.24663 Table 3 scores a one-token opening only on base and final RL (Qwen3-4B-Base, AIME: 10.00 -> 13.23, RL 19.32, 35 % of the gain); 2610.06851 App. D Fig. 14 trains RL with the cue forced (reaches plain RL's step-300 accuracy in 100 steps) and Fig. 16 gives opening probabilities before and after RL only. No paper scores plain and cued prompts, or the opening's probability, at intermediate checkpoints of plain RL. (2) Vote-reward RL from a base model is published, without token matching: 2511.04902 Table 1, MATH-500, Qwen2.5 base: 7B 58.2 -> vote 73.6 vs labelled 73.8; 3B 54.2 -> 63.8 vs 64.4; 0.5B collapses to 0.0 vs 33.8. TTRL 2504.16084: Qwen2.5-7B 60.5 -> 80.5. So a no-label reward equals a labelled one when the start model is right often enough, and fails when it is not. (3) Tinker (Thinking Machines) serves no Olmo model; its base models are Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B-Base and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base; its cookbook RL loop defaults to the 9B base, LoRA rank 32, lr 4e-5. A ready study for the per-checkpoint curve there (spec, RL loop with grader or vote reward, eval, readout, offline run passed, no model call yet) is on branch tinker, studies/tinkerpair/specs/SPEC.md; it waits on account billing. idea-035a30

Theory round 05, refuted theories (each by a number computed from stored rows; studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v4.json): (1) grader v3 false negatives explain part of the hard328 gap: numeric equivalence recovers 0 of the cued base's finished v3-wrong non-integer answers, gap stays 12.8 points. (2) the cued base overwrites a right first answer: 0 of its v3-wrong MATH-500 answers have a right first marker. Activation edits during generation run inside vLLM 0.32 at vLLM speed, no Hugging Face generate needed. vLLM serves Olmo 3 through its Transformers backend, so model.model.layers[l] are the Hugging Face blocks and a torch forward hook on a block acts on every sequence of the batch (hidden state [1, tokens of all running requests, 4096]). Needed: VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 (model in the job's process), EngineArgs(enforce_eager=True) (a Python hook is not replayed by a CUDA graph), enable_prefix_caching=False when arms differ in activations; find the model by walking the engine's attributes (vLLM freezes the gc list). Per-request logit_bias works with seeded sampling. Instrument check to copy: a huge edit must change every answer (alpha 8 gave only 'wait' tokens). Measured: 17 arms x 63 problems x 1,024 tokens in 11 minutes on one H100; a 500-problem arm at cap 16,384 in 31 to 35 minutes, the same as run_cell; a random direction of 6.8 % of the block norm scores 409/500 (stored unsteered cells 404 to 418). From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 loop detectors): use the zlib rule (rule A), not a period rule or a repeated-line count, to call base-model loops. Rule A: an 8,000-character window starting at a line start with zlib compression ratio < 0.10; onset = first line of the repeated block. Tested on saved MATH-500 answers (T 0.6, cap 16,384): fires on 0 of 484 RL finished answers, 1 of 431 base plain (n13), 0 of 435 and 0 of 381 for two base-01 cells; fires on 59 of 60, 46 of 48 and 90 of 92 low-ratio cap hits. Rule B (period <= 64 characters over >= 2,000 characters, 3 cycles; as relayed from arXiv 2611.06095, paper not read) has no false positives but catches only 6-17 % of the loops, because the base's loops have periods of hundreds of characters. A crude rule (any line > 20 characters three times) fires on 60 of 484 RL finished answers, so it fails. Caveat: on low-ratio cap hits rule A's hit rate is nearly guaranteed by construction; the test is the false-positive side, and the onset was checked by eye on 4 answers only. At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3 (500 each); the cued base at T 0.6 has 92 low-ratio cap hits of 119. Status: closed instrument check, not audited. Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/rln4/offline/prep_checks.json (detector), SPEC4.md section 4; code iterate-hack studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py onset_lines.

From interp_research bytegraft (how small a fitted patch carries a skill, and whether an LLM editor finds it; complements result-6199f4 and knowledge-c9fc18): S = Bolmo-1B-Stage1 lacks a CUTE word-edit skill that its fine-tune Bolmo-1B has. On 2,400 held-out check items (S 14.42): a rank-1 LoRA fitted on all 112 matrices (753,664 numbers) reads 32.04 and beats an LLM editor's 8.5M-number neuron patch by +6.50 [4.83, 8.21]. LLM editor against a gradient-ranked neuron set of matched size: -0.75 [-2.71, 1.21]. At about 1M neurons the gradient ranking reads 22.12 and random neurons 18.08. The editor's +1.42 lead over a scripted top-32 falls to +0.46 [-0.71, 1.62] at a matched seed. LLM agents choosing attention heads to patch: 0.394 and 0.363 against gradient ranking 0.356 and a script given the same evidence table 0.375. No LLM-editor advantage over a gradient ranking or a script is shown; the gain comes from fitting, not from the chosen support: F's values copied onto the editor's or the gradient ranking's support with no fit lower the host (16.42 and 17.92 against 22.00). Character edits stay at 10 % or below under every patch. Transfer trap: a patch fitted without F still raises OLMo-2-0425-1B by +8.00, so 'patch transfers to another host' measured the shared interface, not the skill. Activation transfer: writing F's attention outputs into S recovers 0.81 of F's advantage (F's MLP writes none); controls (no-skill donor scaled to F's size 0.195, another item's writes 0.031) pass, but this is the donor running in parallel, not a weight graft. Status: closed, owner's verdict 'just LoRA'; audits AUDIT f, g, h, h2. Lesson for the RL gap: report a fitted low-rank arm and a gradient-ranked arm before crediting any hand- or LLM-chosen patch. From interp_research neuronoff (single-neuron ablation effect sizes; complements work-383069): zeroing one MLP neuron at one sign of its activation in Qwen3-4B-Base (156 neurons) and gemma-3-4b-pt (202) moves NLL on that neuron's own top contexts by a median 0.0026-0.0093 nats per side; the per-context median is at most 0.000037 nats. Zeroing a whole layer moves the median context by 0.014 (Qwen) and 0.021 (gemma) nats. The per-neuron positive control (a 0.05-nat floor) failed on 65/156 and 75/202 neurons, so every label was cancelled. Behaviour test on 7 hand-picked neurons: 0 of 7 changed generated text when zeroed. Status: closed and reviewed (a different model recomputed it from raw banks); cancelled by its own gate. Lesson: one neuron's necessity is about 0.01 nats on its own contexts, below a per-neuron floor of 0.05; a neuron-level test on Olmo-3 needs a pooled positive control checked for room, at least 30 held-out contexts per neuron, and the Olmo off-target null (instruments item). Artifact: interp_research studies/neuronoff/CLOSEOUT.md (claims N2, N12, N13), results/RESULTS.md section 3.

From interp_research mechanics (Olmo-3 internals; complements work-383069, relevant to the base's loops at T 0.6 in result-dadeec): on Olmo-3-1025-7B final weights, 512 repeated random-token sequences, 1,336 MLP neurons rise on the second pass by at least 0.2 of their 99.9th-percentile scale and 1,237 fall by as much (null max 0.055), about 2,600 of 352,256. 99.5 % sit at or after layer 7, the first induction-head layer (top detector head L15 H5); counts peak at layers 10-15 (121-171 per layer) with a second group of 60 in layers 29-31. Removing the top 8 induction heads leaves 0.771 [0.706, 0.839] of the top-100 neurons' repeat response (8 random heads leave 0.980), so the response is spread over more than 8 heads. The top-100 neurons' strongest corpus passages are literal repeats (text, code, repeated row formats) 8x [4, 12] as often as layer-matched random neurons' (0.16 vs 0.02). On rare random tokens the median neuron runs at 0.72 of its natural-text activity: 2.96x in layers 0-1, 0.36x in layers 26-31. From interp_research instruments (E1, E1b, E5, E6b; complements work-383069 and result-156f7b): on Olmo-3-1025-7B, writing a replacement value into a set of ~50 earlier-layer MLP neurons also moves a target neuron on contexts unrelated to that set, an off-target term absent in gemma and Qwen. Measured with 56 fake two-neuron pairs as the ratio of off-target fall to own fall (null should be 0): mean replacement 0.163 with all neurons eligible, 0.067 [0.034, 0.089] with the always-on neurons excluded; zero with exclusion 0.007 [-0.002, 0.032]; median 0.049; resample 0.147 (worst). Own falls are 0.42-0.48 under every value, so the value choice moves only the off-target part. gemma-3-4b-pt 0.004 and Qwen3-4B-Base 0.003 (no term). OLMo-2-1124-7B 0.123 [0.087, 0.169] against Olmo-3's 0.128 like for like: the term belongs to the OLMo lineage, not to Olmo-3's training run. Candidate causes, not separated: no input norms (output norms only), QK-norm over the whole projection, d 4096, MHA, untied embeddings. The term travels through the other window positions: writing only at the measured token leaves 0.005 [0.002, 0.010] against 0.074. Always-on neurons = top 1 % by mean activation (3,412); the ones that act are a few dozen mid-layer outliers at ~145x their layer's median |activation|. Rule for Olmo-3: zero (or write at the measured token only) with always-on neurons excluded; never mean replacement; on any OLMo model measure a random-set null first. Ablation results from Qwen or gemma papers do not transfer to Olmo without that null. Status: closed 2026-11-05, every stage read by a different model (errata E1b-b, E1b-f, E5-b, E6b-a to h). Artifact: interp_research studies/instruments/results/RESULTS.md Results 4-8, 18-19, 28-34; e1/verdict_e1.json, e1b/verdict_e1b.json, e5/verdict_e5.json, e6/verdict_e6b.json.

From interp_research instruments E2 (a check of the Weight-Space Programming loop edit, complements knowledge-c9fc18 and result-6199f4): we re-ran the released Qwen3.5-0.8B edit (the editor's direction projected out of 64 MLP-out columns in each of layers 15 and 19, strength 6) beside random-column controls. 300 MATH-500 problems, one sample, 8,192-token cap, presence penalty 1.5. Accuracy: base 14/300 (4.7 %), released edit 33/300 (11.0 %), one random column set matched on weight norm 28/300 (9.3 %), one matched on KL 30/300 (10.0 %). Edit minus norm-matched random: +1.7 points [-1.7, +5.0], not separated. Cap hits: base 95 %, edit 88 %, random 90 %. The edit is specific on loops: the share of answers with a repeated 10-gram falls by 0.317 [0.247, 0.383] under the edit and by 0.08-0.09 under random columns. Columns ranked by alignment with the editor's direction reproduce it (64 columns 0.307, 256 columns 0.377), but that direction is the edit's own singular vector, so no weights-only discovery is shown. A KL-matched random control was no stricter than a norm-matched one. Status: exploratory; the frozen room gate cancelled every rule (cut share 0.96; the editor's own 32,768-token eval also cuts 93 % of base answers); one random draw only. Lesson for base + a*(RL - base) (work-d36669): on a cap-limited model a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain; report a random-direction arm, cap hits and loops beside accuracy. Published, do not run on a plain base (papers read in full, texts in papers/): (a) power sampling / MCMC: +2.4 to +3.5 points on MATH-500, 18-27 % of the RL gain, none on AIME (2610.24663 Table 1). (b) Fixed rules: forced 'Wait', logit bias, greedy first 100 tokens, entropy stop, longer prefill: at or below base (2610.24663 Tables 3, 5, App. G). (c) Majority vote: plain base stays below RL for 24 of 24 decoding policies at every N up to 16 on Qwen2.5-7B / MATH-500 (2609.01274 Fig. 8b). Maj@4 adds 0.8 points to a 73.6 % model on MATH500; best-of-n by self-confidence is below one sample (2507.18122 Table 1). (d) Loop penalties: DRY costs 14.2 points on MATH-500 for Qwen3-4B (2610.24715 Table 16). (e) Top-p vs temperature: removing top-p at T 0.6 cuts limit loops 59 -> 53, T 1 cuts to 24 (Qwen3-4B, 360 structured generations, not math; 2610.24715 Table 9). (f) RL gain is sparse: RL's greedy token at the 4 % of positions where greedy tokens differ recovers 90.5 % of the gain on AIME; base entropy finds those positions with AUROC 0.94-0.98; RL's token has mean rank 2.1-2.4 in the base (2610.24663 Table 3, App. E; 2605.06241 Table 2). No label-free rule is published that picks the right token there. (g) Label-free training (entropy minimization, vote reward) closes 80-100 % of the gap on Math-500 and 0-70 % on AIME for Qwen2.5-Math-7B (2505.15134 Table 2); vote reward collapses near 1,000 steps (2603.08660). result-04e329.title: The 1.5x RL-direction edit holds on unseen 2026 problems
result-04e329.what: The base plus 1.5 times the 8 strongest directions of RL's weight change was sampled four times on 136 problems published in 2026: 50, 52, 45, 46 right, mean 48.25. RL has 50.5 and the base with the cue 29.5.
result-04e329.why: The edit's size was picked on the 328 harder problems. Here nothing was chosen, and it stays within 1.7 points of RL [-5.3, 1.8] and 13.8 above the base. All three predictions filed before the run hold.
result-04e329.caveat: The edit is built from the RL checkpoint's weights, so it is not a route without reward. Under the vote it has 53 against RL's 57 (-2.9 points [-8.1, 2.2]).

result-1a80e9.title: The cue found on math also works outside math and code

result-1b6bf2.title: RL's directions lengthen short answers and cut the tail
result-1b6bf2.what: From stored rows of the edit cells on 328 hard problems: answer lengths against the base on problems both finish, right answers within a token budget, and a restart of unfinished problems with the twice-size edit.

result-284db5.title: 8 RL directions per matrix lift the base on harder problems
result-284db5.what: On 328 harder problems, adding the top 8 directions of each matrix's RL weight change to the cued base scored 192, against 164 for the base, 158 for random directions and 206 for RL. RL with those 8 removed scored 190.
result-284db5.why: The 8 directions cut answers hitting the length cap (77 to 46) and raise words like Wait to RL's rate. The rest of the RL change raises accuracy too, but loops more than the base.

result-296647.title: Tuning the base on its own voted answers adds nothing
result-296647.what: The base was fine-tuned on its own MATH-500 answers picked by a vote over samples, with no correct answers used. On 328 harder problems with the cue it scored 167, against 164 untuned and 168 when tuned on random own answers.

result-306787.title: Finishing and right answers split by rank and by depth
result-306787.what: Shrank the 1.5x edit of the base two ways on 328 hard problems with the cue: one direction per matrix at 2x and 3x, and the 8 directions at 1.5x in layers 0-10, 11-21 or 22-31 only.
result-306787.why: The first direction and the late layers cut cap hits without adding right answers; the early layers add right answers while cap hits rise to 98, so 0.80 of their finished answers are right.
result-306787.caveat: One sample per cell, differences under about 5 points are not resolved. Both filed predictions were refuted; the split by depth was read after the run.

result-3387ce.title: Twice the RL weight change on Think-SFT: 231.5 of 328
result-3387ce.what: Think-SFT + a x (RL-Math - base), cue, hard328, T 1.0, v3. a=2 scores 234 and 229 (two seeds), +6.9 pts [4.6, 9.3] over Think-SFT (209.0, 4 samples) and +9.6 [6.9, 12.3] over RL (200.0). a=1 220, a=3 227, a=4 213.
result-3387ce.why: The RL change makes Think-SFT finish: cap hits 94.5, 75, 54, 44, 33 for a = 0..4, while right-of-finished falls 88 to 72 %. Right answers peak at a=2. Noise of the same norm changes nothing (209, 97 cap). MATH-500 a=1: 467, as filed.
result-3387ce.caveat: One sample for a=1, 3, 4 and the control; a=0.5 hung twice, no number. The coefficient was chosen on the 328 itself (second seed pre-registered). Summing SFT and RL vectors is published (2605.00610); the dose curve and control are new.

result-34897a.title: Entropy-gated temperature does not beat plain T 1.0
result-34897a.what: Base + cue on MATH-500: T 0.6 only at confident positions (entropy <= 0.9 nats), only at forks, or everywhere except after a repeat. All three score 1.3 to 1.4 points under plain T 1.0 (410.5/500), intervals through 0.
result-34897a.why: Cap hits per 500: T 1.0 22.5, forks only 33, confident only 44, both (T 0.6) 98; adding the two gives 55, so loops need both regimes sharpened. Removing randomness trades accuracy of finished answers for loops. Not run on the 328.
result-34897a.caveat: T 0.6 is one stored sample; the repeat-aware cell has 1 sample (the second was lost in a box teardown); score lines round the means 403.5 to 404. Intervals: -1.4 [-3.2, 0.4], -1.4 [-3.5, 0.8], -1.3 [-4.3, 1.5].

result-39497c.title: Dial controls hold: random and Think-SFT edits do nothing

result-3a3af3.title: The base reaches the cue's score with no cue prefilled
result-3a3af3.what: On MATH-500 the untrained base drew up to 32 openings of 24 tokens per problem at T 1.0 and continued the first one that opens with a newline then 'Okay'; nothing was prefilled.
result-3a3af3.why: Choosing among the base's own first tokens gives the whole gain of the opening cue, so the cue adds no information the base does not already produce.
result-3a3af3.caveat: One sample per problem; shards ran on two GPU types; 94 problems keep their stored plain answer, which already opened this way.

result-40ed3b.title: No reward-free base rule reaches one RL sample on MATH-500
result-40ed3b.what: 24 rules for combining up to 4 base samples were fixed before scoring. The best, a vote after restarts, scored 454 of 500 with 4.2 times the tokens of one RL sample (460). RL under the same rules stays ahead, at 474.5.
result-40ed3b.caveat: The best rule's gap to one RL sample, 1.2 points, lies within its 95 % interval, and the harder problems were not yet scored.

result-44b4df.title: Cutting the sampling tail does not help at temperature 1
result-44b4df.what: Min-p and top-p truncation at temperature 1.0 scored 404 to 412 of 500 for the cued base, within noise of untruncated sampling (410). RL moved by +0.6 points.
result-44b4df.why: Truncating the tail brings repetition loops back: loops went from 0 to 34 at min-p 0.1, and length-cap hits from 27 to 58.
result-44b4df.caveat: One sample per setting. Two samples of one setting disagree on 76 to 85 problems, so gains under about 3.5 points cannot be seen.

result-460e0a.title: Loop-neuron edit shows no score gain on a second seed
result-460e0a.what: On a second seed at temperature 0.6, zeroing 100 or 1,000 loop-linked neurons in the cued base scored 398 and 399 of 500 against 394 unedited, with up to 19 % fewer tokens. At temperature 1.0 it scored 390 and 372 against 410.
result-460e0a.why: The edit removes loops (61 down to 18 and 9), which occur only at 0.6. That lifts the 0.6 setting to about the level of the unedited model at 1.0, where there are no loops to remove.
result-460e0a.caveat: The earlier gain from 378 to 414 was mostly seed noise: the unedited run alone moves 16 problems between seeds. The temperature 1.0 numbers are unpaired totals.

result-4b0d5f.title: A quarter of the RL weight change gives most of the gain
result-4b0d5f.what: Adding a fraction of the RL-minus-base weight change to the base: with the cue, a quarter scores 441/500 against 410, and more stays at 450 to 457. A random change of equal size scores 417; the Code-RL change 450.
result-4b0d5f.caveat: After rounding, the quarter blend carries 0.42 of the full change's size. Steps from one half on are within the base's spread of 405 to 418 over 5 runs.

result-51a0e7.title: RL's top directions: more finished answers, more right ones
result-51a0e7.what: Added 1, 8 or 64 top singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math minus base) to the base, at 1x and 2x size, by module family and split by Code 3.0's input subspace; scored on 328 hard problems with the cue.
result-51a0e7.why: Cap hits follow the size of the 8 directions (RL minus them 90, base 77, eight 46, 2x 5). On the 251 problems the base finishes, eight directions also add right answers: 175 against 161.
result-51a0e7.caveat: One sample per cell. Earlier title 'finish, not be right' was wrong: half of the gain is on problems the base already finishes (+5.6 pts [0.8, 10.8]); only the step from 1x to 2x adds finishing alone.

result-51ccc6.title: The depth split of the dial does not hold on code
result-51ccc6.what: Tested a reading made after the math run (early layers add right answers, late layers make the model finish): RL-Code's 8 directions at 1.5x in layers 0-10, 11-21 or 22-31 only, on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with the Code cue.
result-51ccc6.caveat: One sample per cell. Two of the three filed predictions were refuted, so the earlier result title 'split by depth' holds for the math cells only.

result-51fd20.title: Forcing long answers to commit loses hard problems
result-51fd20.what: Cutting the cued base's answers at 8,000 tokens and forcing a final boxed answer scored 152 of 328 harder problems, against 164 when left to run, while using about a third fewer tokens.
result-51fd20.why: Answers that hit the length cap are failures to solve: a forced answer is right on at most 2 of the 77 that hit it, and a hand read found most forced answers were guesses.

result-5227b9.title: Examples in context do not move the base toward RL
result-5227b9.what: Three solved answers written by the RL model were put before each prompt to the base. A first set gave +5.7 points on MATH-500; a second set gave -0.6 (401 vs 404 of 494), and the first set gave 164 vs 164 on 328 harder problems.
result-5227b9.caveat: Only two sets of 3 examples were tried, and why the two sets differ by 6.3 points is not explained.

result-5251c9.title: Think-SFT's lead over RL holds on 2026 problems
result-5251c9.what: Three models on 136 contest problems first published in 2026, after all their weights existed: Think-SFT with the cue, RL-Zero-Math, and the untrained base with the cue; 4 samples and a vote.
result-5251c9.why: Think-SFT hits the token cap on 46 % of samples and is right in 80 % of the answers it finishes; RL finishes 85 % and is right in 43 %, so wrong answers outvote its right ones.
result-5251c9.caveat: 77 of the 136 statements were transcribed from the official PDFs by a language model; n = 136 gives an interval of about 6 points each way; contests can reuse older problems (one found and dropped).

result-59ed1a.title: On code, the cue recovers over half of the RL gain
result-59ed1a.what: On 538 coding problems (HumanEval+ and MBPP+), one sample each, programs passing: plain base 222, base with the Code cue 317, base with the Math cue 326, code RL model 401. The cue gives the base 53 to 58 % of the RL gain.
result-59ed1a.why: The Code cue and the Math cue are different texts that both end in "Okay", and they score equally. The study concludes that the opening word and a reasoning start are what help, rather than the text before it.
result-59ed1a.caveat: The code RL model stays 13.9 to 15.6 points ahead of the cued base at equal tokens per problem. On MATH-500 the cue recovers 78 % of the gain. The vote over 4 samples after restart was not run.

result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#222/538.title: Starting point on code: the base model, plain prompt
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#222/538.what: The untrained base model writes one program for each of 538 coding problems (HumanEval+ and MBPP+) from the plain prompt, with no cue. 222 programs pass their tests (41.3 %). The RL model trained for code passes 401.
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#222/538.caveat: One sample per problem. 4 of the 542 problems are excluded because their reference solution fails the grader check. 43 of the base's answers contain no code block.

result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#317/538.title: Add the code model's own 12-token opening as a cue
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#317/538.what: The base model's answer is started with the 12 tokens that the code RL model opens its own answers with, ending in "Okay". Passing programs go from 222 to 317 of 538, a gain of 17.7 points (95 % interval 12.8 to 22.5).
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#317/538.why: The Code cue and the Math cue are different texts that both end in "Okay", and they score equally. The study concludes that the opening word and a reasoning start are what help, rather than the text before it.
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#317/538.caveat: The cue recovers 53 % of the code RL gain, against 78 % on MATH-500, and the RL model stays 15.6 points ahead at equal tokens per problem. One sample per problem; the vote was not run.

result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#326/538.title: Swap in the three-token Math cue
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#326/538.what: The 12-token Code cue is replaced by the three-token Math cue, the one used on MATH-500, taken from the math RL model's answers. Passing programs go from 317 to 326 of 538.
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#326/538.why: The result treats the two cues as equal: Code cue minus Math cue is -1.7 points, with a 95 % interval from -5.8 to +2.8. Both cues end in the word "Okay" and start the model reasoning.
result-59ed1a#HumanEval+MBPP+#326/538.caveat: The 95 % interval of the difference between the two cues includes zero, so the 9-problem gain does not show that the Math cue is better. One sample per problem.

result-5c961a.title: Harder 328: the vote narrows the gap to RL, not closes it
result-5c961a.what: Each model answered the 328 harder problems four times, again after a cut-off answer; the most common answer was graded. Base with cue 195 of 328, RL 224. RL minus base 8.8 points [5.5, 12.5]; one sample: 14.0.
result-5c961a.why: The procedure was fixed on MATH-500 and nothing was chosen on the 328, so this is the held-out reading of the vote result. RL stays ahead under every rule tried.
result-5c961a.caveat: The shortest-answer tie-break does not hold up here (191 against the vote's 192), so its 453 on MATH-500 was chosen in-sample; quote the plain vote.

result-5d032f.title: A vote over 4 samples lifts the base to 89 %, RL still leads
result-5d032f.what: At T 1.0, both models answer each MATH-500 problem 4 times. The vote takes the base with cue from 405 to 446 of 500 and the RL model from 456 to 474. Restarting cap hits adds 8 problems alone and 4 on top of the vote.
result-5d032f.why: The vote turned 43 base problems from wrong to right and 2 the other way: the single sample had been wrong 28 times and without an answer 15 times. A restart lets a cap hit finish and cast a vote.
result-5d032f.caveat: The base's vote uses 3.4 times the tokens of one RL sample and is still 2.0 points below it (95 % interval -4.0 to 0.2). About 1 point of a vote row is run-to-run variation. An audit recount reproduced the scores.

result-5d032f#MATH-500#446/500.title: Answer each problem 4 times and take a vote
result-5d032f#MATH-500#446/500.what: Back at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, the base with cue answers every problem 4 times and the most common answer is taken: a vote over 4 samples, with no restart. One sample at this setting gets 405 of 500, the vote 446.
result-5d032f#MATH-500#446/500.why: The vote turned 43 problems from wrong to right and 2 from right to wrong. In the 43, the single sample had a wrong answer 28 times and no answer 15 times (10 of them cap hits).
result-5d032f#MATH-500#446/500.caveat: It costs about 4 times the tokens per problem (16,034 against 3,808 for one sample). The RL model also gains from the vote (456 to 474) and stays 5.6 points ahead.

result-5d032f#MATH-500#450/500.title: Retry answers that ran out of length, then vote
result-5d032f#MATH-500#450/500.what: Each of the 4 samples that is a cap hit is restarted first: sampled again, up to twice, keeping the first attempt that finishes. The vote over 4 samples then runs as before. Right answers go from 446 to 450 of 500.
result-5d032f#MATH-500#450/500.why: A sample with no final answer casts no vote. A restart gives a cap hit another chance to finish: of the first sample's 25 cap hits, 8 ended right, 8 ended wrong and 9 hit the cap all three times.
result-5d032f#MATH-500#450/500.caveat: The gain is 4 problems (0.8 points), and the study puts run-to-run variation of a vote row at about 1 point. Tokens per problem rise from 16,034 to 19,697. An audit names 450 the honest best base score.

result-6832a8.title: Four samples: 100 RL steps within 3.3 points of the cue
result-6832a8.what: AI2's RL checkpoints on MATH-500, T 1.0, now four samples per cell. Step 100 plain 417.5 of 500 against 410.5 for the untrained base with the cue: +1.40 points [-0.50, +3.25]. Step 100 with the cue 426.0, step 400 437.75, final 460.0.
result-6832a8.why: 'Equals' is not earned: the interval includes 0 but ends outside the filed [-3, +3] band. Step 100 with the cue leads the cued base by +3.10 [+1.45, +4.70], so the cue and the first 100 steps are not interchangeable.
result-6832a8.caveat: Interval over problems only (per-problem mean of 4 samples); one benchmark, one model family. Cue on step 100: +1.70 [0.00, +3.35], borderline.

result-6d422d.title: RL-written examples gave +5.6 points once; it did not repeat
result-6d422d.what: Three solved answers written by the RL model, placed before each prompt, raised the cued base on MATH-500 from 407 to 435 of 497. Examples written by the base or by a code-trained RL model gave no clear gain.
result-6d422d.caveat: Later correction: a second set of 3 RL-written examples gave 401 vs 404, and the first set gave no gain on 328 harder problems.

result-6de887.title: Zeroing 1,000 loop neurons cuts loops but not errors
result-6de887.what: Turning off 1,000 neurons (0.28 %) linked to repetition loops in the cued base cut looping answers from 71 to 19 and tokens per problem by 17 %. Right answers moved only from 378 to 381 of 500.
result-6de887.why: A removed loop only gives one more attempt at a hard problem: of the 71 looped problems, 33 were right with the edit and 25 with 1,000 random neurons zeroed.
result-6de887.caveat: Per an audit, the neurons were ranked on 14 of the 500 problems, and the random control is not matched on normal-text loss (+8.2 % vs +0.3 %).

result-6f1bb7.title: A 0.11% weight edit takes the base to RL's score
result-6f1bb7.what: Added the top 8 singular directions per matrix of (RL-Math minus base) to the base at sizes -1 to 3, with a random rank-8 edit at the same sizes, and the 8 directions of other rewards; 328 hard problems with the cue.
result-6f1bb7.why: Cap hits fall with the size of the 8 directions (96 at -1, 77 base, 46 at 1, 25 at 1.5, 5 at 2) and right answers on problems the base already finishes rise (113, 161, 175, 184); the random edit stays at 67-79 cap hits.
result-6f1bb7.caveat: One sample per cell: 203 at size 1.5 against 192 at size 1 is +3.4 pts [-0.9, 7.6], and 1.5 was one of seven sizes tried. At size 3 the model decays into word strings (117 right).

result-6f7ca3.title: Math depth and rank split holds: 7 of 7 predictions
result-6f7ca3.what: Base Olmo 3 + Math 3.1's top-8 directions at 1.5x, restricted to layer bands or to directions 2-8, on hard328 (cue, T 1.0, cap 16,384), 1-4 samples per cell, paired bootstrap over problems.
result-6f7ca3.why: Tests whether early layers add right answers, late layers only cut cap hits, and direction 1 alone does the finishing.

result-6f7ca3#hard328#162/328.caveat: Math only; on Code the depth split was refuted (result-51ccc6). New cells and controls have 1 sample, L11-21/L22-31 have 2. 818 H100-min.

result-79784b.title: Switching off loop neurons adds no right answers on hard set
result-79784b.what: Zeroing 100 or 1,000 loop-linked neurons in the cued base gave 155 and 130 of 328 harder problems at temperature 1.0, against 164 unedited. At temperature 0.6 it gave 149, against 134 unedited.
result-79784b.why: The edit turns answers that would run to the length cap into finished wrong answers (cap hits 77 to 47 and 32). At 0.6 it removes loops (94 to 24 and 6), but still stays below the unedited model at 1.0.
result-79784b.caveat: Repeats of the unedited run range from 155 to 168, so 155 is within noise; the gain at 0.6 has an interval of 0.0 to 9.1 points.

result-818c20.title: Imitation-trained model with a vote beats RL on the 328
result-818c20.what: Think-SFT with the opening cue, four samples and a vote: 241 of 328 hard problems, against 221 for the RL model and 192 for the untrained base under the same vote.
result-818c20.why: It is the best configuration found that uses no reward. It wins because it runs out of tokens instead of giving a wrong answer, so its votes are rarely wrong.

result-82b4dc.title: On 328 harder problems RL leads the cued base by 13 points
result-82b4dc.what: Both models answer 328 harder problems, all absent from the RL training set, once each at temperature 1.0. The base with cue gets 164 (50.0 %) and the RL model 206 (62.8 %), at equal tokens per problem (9,345 and 9,316).
result-82b4dc.why: 77 of the base's 328 answers are cap hits, against 20 for the RL model, and only 3 of the 77 are scored right. At this setting the base's cap hits are long reasoning that does not repeat, rather than loops.
result-82b4dc.caveat: One sample per problem. The gap of 12.8 points has a 95 % interval of 8.5 to 17.1. An audit read 164 from the committed readout only, because the raw answers are not in the repository.

result-82b4dc#hard328#164/328.title: Starting point on the 328 harder problems
result-82b4dc#hard328#164/328.what: The base with the opening cue answers each of the 328 harder problems once, at temperature 1.0, and gets 164 right (50.0 %). The RL-trained model gets 206 (62.8 %) with the same number of tokens per problem.

result-854ca8.title: Signed self-training with no reward loses points
result-854ca8.what: One LoRA epoch on the base's 4 stored samples per MATH-500 problem, raising the samples that agree with the vote and lowering the others (arm P), or the same with the answer key (arm G), then the cue on hard328 (n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample).
result-854ca8.why: RL's update is signed; SFT on voted samples was not. Neither the sign nor the key helps offline: answers stop finishing (cap hits 77 -> 178 / 145, no loops, Wait doubles); where both finish, accuracy is equal.
result-854ca8.caveat: one epoch, stored samples only, no resampling. Held-out NLL gap wrong-minus-right did not rise.

result-882fa7.title: Making the base say Wait as often as RL does not help
result-882fa7.what: Steering the cued base's activations until it writes Wait and Hmm at RL's rate (8.3 per 1,000 tokens) scored 413 of 500, against 410.5 unsteered and 409 for a random push. RL scores 457; a stronger push fell to 381.
result-882fa7.why: The added Waits are mostly filler: a blind reader called 16 of 20 filler and 1 a fix, against 7 fixes in 20 of the model's own. The word is a trace of RL's checking habit rather than its cause.
result-882fa7.caveat: One sample per setting, with a spread of about 7 problems; the unsteered run in the same job scored 430, read as a high draw, and a second seed was still running.

result-95a4dc.title: The 1.5x RL-direction edit matches RL on new samples
result-95a4dc.what: The base plus 1.5 times the 8 strongest directions of RL's weight change was sampled four times on the 328 harder problems: 207, 198, 199, 197 right, mean 200.25 against RL's 200.0. On MATH-500 one sample has 456 of 500 against RL's 457.
result-95a4dc.why: The first 203 was one sample at a size picked on the 328. New samples and the held-out MATH-500 cell confirm it. Under the vote over 4 the edit has 214 against RL's 221, so it does not fully match RL there.

result-96e819.title: A self-review pass fixes no math for base or RL
result-96e819.what: Each cued answer got one appended pass in which the model reviews its own work. The base went from 410 to 415 of 500 and RL from 457 to 454, once a grader misread was removed.
result-96e819.why: 6 of the base's 7 fixes repaired the answer's format and only 1 fixed math. RL fixed none of its 35 wrong answers and broke 3.
result-96e819.caveat: The grader misread (it took 'the answer is correct.' as the answer) was removed after looking at the data, for both models.

result-997be4.title: No text sign predicts a failing Think-SFT sample early
result-997be4.what: Six label-free text signs read at token 4,000 to 12,000 do not tell a failing Think-SFT sample from a right one of the same problem: best AUROC 0.568 [0.480, 0.657]. Stopping at the first sign saves 0.8 % of tokens on hard328, not 10 %.
result-997be4.why: Cap hits are 29 to 46 % of Think-SFT's samples; a perfect detector at token 4,000 would give 244 of 328 at 16,250 tokens against 241 at 30,837. Text signs do not provide it (as result-f3d708, result-b30f15).
result-997be4.caveat: Replay on stored rows, not a new run. One hand reader. The 32,768 result is one sample per problem. Only 29 samples have switched by token 8,000.

result-997be4#hard328#240/328.what: The stop rule chosen on MATH-500, replayed on the stored four samples; the plain sequential vote has 241 at 30,904.
result-997be4#hard328#240/328.caveat: A stopped sample casts no vote and the next sample is the next stored one.

result-a1bf75.title: The finish dial holds on a second model pair: code
result-a1bf75.what: Added the 8 largest directions per matrix of (RL-Code minus base) to the base at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, a random edit at 1.5x, and RL-Math's directions at 1.5x; scored on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ (538 problems) with the Code cue.

result-a74ac3.title: Base without the cue: 10 of 136 fresh 2026 problems
result-a74ac3.what: Cell m20: Olmo-3-1025-7B base, plain prompt (no cue), fresh2026, 1 sample, T 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. 10 right [5, 15] (90 %), 13 cap hits. The 23 answers that open with 'Okay' unprompted give 6 of the 10. With the cue: 28-32.

result-ad3c24.title: 8 directions per matrix carry most of the RL gain

result-bce075.title: Handing a Think-SFT answer to RL to finish gains nothing

result-bce075.why: RL stops where Think-SFT would run out of tokens, but it stops on a wrong answer: on the 89 cap-hit prefixes both finishers get 16 to 18 right.

result-c36598.title: The opening cue takes the base from 45 % to 82 %
result-c36598.what: On MATH-500 at temperature 1.0, the untrained base model gets 224 of 500 right from the plain prompt and 410 of 500 when its answer is started with a three-token cue copied from the RL-trained model's answers.
result-c36598.why: The RL-trained model writes this opening by itself. The study's reading, from a code test where two different cues that both end in "Okay" scored equally, is that the opening word and a reasoning start are what help.
result-c36598.caveat: Against the plain base's better setting (319 of 500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95) the gain is smaller. A rerun on the same seeds gave 405 rather than 410, and 27 of the cued answers are cap hits.

result-c36598#MATH-500#224/500.title: Starting point: the untrained base model, plain prompt
result-c36598#MATH-500#224/500.what: The untrained base model (Olmo 3) answers each of the 500 MATH-500 problems once from the plain prompt, with no opening cue, at temperature 1.0 (AI2's own sampling setting). It gets 224 right (44.8 %).
result-c36598#MATH-500#224/500.caveat: This is the plain base's weaker setting: at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 it gets 319 of 500. An audit did not recount 224, because the raw answers are not in the repository.

result-c36598#MATH-500#410/500.what: The base model's answer is started for it with a cue: three tokens ending in the word "Okay", copied from the way the RL-trained model opens its own answers. Nothing else changes. Right answers go from 224 to 410 of 500.

result-c8b994.title: Twice the token cap gives Think-SFT 23 more problems
result-c8b994.what: Think-SFT cue and RL plain on hard328 with the cap at 32,768 instead of 16,384 generated tokens (n 328, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, v3, 1 sample, seed 3000000). Each run is also scored at 16,384 from the same answers.
result-c8b994.why: Think-SFT's cut answers are unfinished work: 91 of 93 finish in the second 16,384 tokens, 23 right, for 1,747 more tokens per problem. RL has 20 long answers and gains 2.
result-c8b994.caveat: base cue at 32,768 was lost with its box; rerunning on AWS. RL's 16,384 score in this run is 193 (stored 206; its 4 stored samples span 190-209).

result-cbe0bc.title: Shortest-answer tie-break adds 7 problems to the vote
result-cbe0bc.what: 11 rules that pick among the 4 stored samples without the answer key were scored against the vote. Sending ties to the shortest finished answer gives the base 453 of 500 against 446. Picking one sample by confidence or length scores lower.
result-cbe0bc.why: Only the 36 problems with a tied vote change. The shortest finished answer is right in 12 of them, against 5 for the old rule and about 7 for a random pick. It fixed 7 problems and broke none.
result-cbe0bc.caveat: Read it as 450: an audit notes the rule was written after reading the 7 problems it fixes. The held-out estimate is 451. The rule is not confirmed on the RL model and is not scored on the 328 harder problems.

result-cbe0bc#MATH-500#453/500.title: Break vote ties with the shortest answer
result-cbe0bc#MATH-500#453/500.what: The vote over 4 samples gets a new tie rule: when answers tie for most common, the shortest finished answer wins, instead of the first sample's answer. Applied to the vote without restart (446 of 500), it fixes 7 problems: 453.
result-cbe0bc#MATH-500#453/500.why: Why a shorter answer is more often right is not known yet. Measured: in the 36 tied votes the shortest finished answer is right 12 times, against 5 for the first sample's answer and about 7 for a random pick.
result-cbe0bc#MATH-500#453/500.caveat: An audit says to count this step as 450 of 500 (90.0 %): the rule was written after reading the 7 problems it fixes, and the held-out estimate is 451. It is 3 above the record of 450 because that record used restarts.

result-d02d46.title: Short top-8 answers are right on easy problems
result-d02d46.what: Base + 1x top-8 RL-Math directions, plain, MATH-500, T 1.0: 3 new samples + the stored one (2,000 answers). Short = 1,000 tokens or fewer, binned by the cued base's solves of 4.
result-d02d46.why: Short answers are right 87.2% where the cued base solves 4 of 4 (252/289); 81% of them sit in that bin. Smooth blend holds; r5-m03-rival refuted: share 17.8% [15.7, 20.0] (pred 10-15), right 82.9% (pred ~50).
result-d02d46.caveat: In bin 4 short answers are wrong 12.8% vs 2.1% for long; 26 of 44 short wrong new answers have no extracted answer (12 empty). New samples on other GPUs than the stored one.

result-d92d4a.title: Switching off loop neurons lifts the cued base to 414/500
result-d92d4a.what: Zeroing 1,000 neurons (0.28 %) tied to repetition loops, ranked from the base's own looping answers, raised the cued base from 378 to 414 of 500 on MATH-500 at temperature 0.6, with 26 % fewer tokens.

result-dadeec.title: Cued base at temperature 0.6 without a top-p cut: 378/500
result-dadeec.what: At temperature 0.6 with no top-p cut, the cued base scored 378/500 (75.6 %): 4.8 points above top-p 0.95 and 6.4 points below temperature 1.0.
result-dadeec.why: At 0.6 the base still loops: 71 answers loop and 98 hit the length cap.

result-dd9239.title: Think-SFT's own chat format ties the raw prompt with the cue
result-dd9239.what: Think-SFT on hard328 prompted through its own chat template (system line, chat markers, <think>) instead of the raw template with the base's 3-token cue. n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample, cap 32,768, also counted at 16,384.
result-dd9239.why: No Think-SFT row had used the format the model was trained in. The two formats tie, so the cue brings out all of Think-SFT on the 328 and the study's Think-SFT rows are not held back by the prompt.

result-e45bf4.title: Weight blends raise the cued base on hard problems
result-e45bf4.what: On 328 harder problems with the cue, base-RL weight blends and the Code-RL model scored 182 to 190, 5.5 to 7.9 points above the base (164) but all below RL (206). On MATH-500 they were within 2.6 points of RL.
result-e45bf4.why: The gap to RL is mostly unfinished answers: the half blend hits the length cap on 73 problems against RL's 20, and on finished problems it is close (188 vs 193).
result-e45bf4.caveat: One sample per problem. The audit asks for a rerun of the unfinished answers with a longer cap or restarts before calling this a ceiling.

result-e5c99c.title: On 328 hard problems, RL leads the cued base by 12.8 points
result-e5c99c.what: On 328 harder problems at temperature 1.0, RL scored 206 and the base with the cue 164. At temperature 0.6 the gap was 25.9 points, with the cued base at 119.
result-e5c99c.why: At temperature 1.0 the base hits the length cap far less often (77 problems instead of 173), so more of its answers finish.

result-e870a1.title: At T 0.6 the cued base loops, and restarts recover it
result-e870a1.what: At T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 the base with cue gets 354 of 500, with 119 cap hits. Restarting each cap hit, up to two more times, and scoring the first attempt that finishes gives 414. The RL model gets 464 at T 0.6.
result-e870a1.why: At this setting the base with cue loops until the 16,384-token cap. A restart gives those problems another chance to finish.
result-e870a1.caveat: With restarts the base is still 10.0 points below the RL model at this setting (95 % interval 7.0 to 13.2). 414 is 4 problems above the 410 that the cue alone gets at T 1.0.

result-e870a1#MATH-500#414/500.title: Lower temperature, retry answers that ran out of length
result-e870a1#MATH-500#414/500.what: The setting changes to T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, where the base with cue gets only 354 because 119 answers are cap hits. Each cap hit is restarted: sampled again, up to two more times, and the first attempt that finishes is scored.
result-e870a1#MATH-500#414/500.why: At T 0.6 the base with cue loops, and 119 of its 500 answers run to the 16,384-token cap. A restart gives those problems another chance to finish, which lifts the score from 354 to 414.
result-e870a1#MATH-500#414/500.caveat: The gain over the step before is 4 problems, at a different setting, and a rerun of that step gave 405 rather than 410. A later summary of the chart calls this step inside its confidence interval.

result-edceef.title: MATH-500 gain follows the math share of the RL reward
result-edceef.what: Five Olmo 3 RL-Zero models trained on different rewards were scored with the cue against the base's 410/500: Math 448, Mix 440, General 429, Code 411, instruction following 377.
result-edceef.why: In the 3.0 releases the gain grows with the share of math in the reward. The instruction-following drop is partly format: 34 of its wrong answers have a broken answer line.
result-edceef.caveat: The 3.1 Code model scores 450 with the cue, so a code reward can give the full gain; the ordering by math share holds for the 3.0 releases only.

result-fc7efc.title: Per attempt, RL guesses more often than the base
